Title:
Untying Prefill and Decode Loops in Looped Language Models

Authors:
Yang Hu

Primary category: cs.CL (Computation and Language)
Cross-list: cs.LG (Machine Learning)

Comments:
32 pages, 13 figures. Code, per-item results and a script that recomputes every number: https://github.com/yanghu819/untying-prefill-decode

License: CC BY 4.0

Abstract (plain text):
Looped language models run a block of layers several times for every token and use the same number of loops to read the prompt (prefill) and to generate each answer token (decode). Yet generation is almost all decoding: on Ouro-2.6B, prefill takes 0.4-2.8% of the time of a chain-of-thought answer, so extra prefill loops are nearly free. We untie the two loop counts, reading the prompt with m loops and decoding each token with n. The released model cannot use the states of a longer prefill, so we add LoopBridge, a small adapter (2.4% of the parameters) with which a decoder with n loops reads the prompt states of any prefill depth m. On Ouro-2.6B with one decode loop, four prefill loops instead of one raise the average over 11 benchmarks from 47.2 to 56.8, and the gain levels off at two to four prefill loops. At the same number of decode loops, LoopBridge beats the original model and models distilled to that depth on the same data; at one decode loop it is also 14.2 points more accurate than the original model in the same measured time (41.2 against 27.0 in about 11 seconds per request). Code: https://github.com/yanghu819/untying-prefill-decode
